## Purpose

What problem does this change solve?

## Evidence

How was the behavior tested, including a failure or negative-control case?

## Data hygiene

- [ ] No client, firm, colleague, tenant, environment, credential, tunnel, or machine-specific data.
- [ ] Examples use synthetic data and repository placeholders.
- [ ] Attribution and third-party notices remain intact.

## Control impact

- [ ] No permissions or execution scope changed.
- [ ] If scope changed, the new boundary and residual risk are documented.
- [ ] A checker change includes a self-test that breaks the checker deliberately.

## Documentation

- [ ] README or relevant documentation updated.
- [ ] CHANGELOG updated when the public behavior changes.
